title: The artifact door refuses a key a record set does not declare
intention: A record set in cairn/tools/artifact/jurisdiction.json may declare 'keys_from': '<commons-relative charter path>#<field>'; write()/write_json() to a JSON record of that set refuses, writing nothing, a body whose top-level keys are not all in that charter field's list, naming each extra key and pointing at the set's log; tickets '*.json' declares keys_from 'tickets/_charter+why.json#plan_fields'.
why: Akien 2026-10-09, verbatim: "the plan is always the 'current what to do' all questions answered, all intentions clear. the questions and the answering of them is in the ticket log." 2026-10-10 he chose the layout "Flat plan + .log.jsonl (Recommended)": tickets/<id>-<slug>.json IS the plan, rewritten in place with no superseded lines, and tickets/<id>-<slug>.log.jsonl beside it is the append-only log, one JSON object per line. Then: "to the best of your ability, get it all closed", all pre-approved through PROVED. Intention: /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-a-ticket-is-a-plan-and-a-log.md. Measured 2026-10-10 (/home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/measurements/2026-10-10-ticket-field-readers.json): 244 top-level fields over 516 tickets, 166 of them read by no non-proof code, so the trail is mostly fields nobody but a reader-mind opens.
traces_to: Law 4 (the plan's field set is enforced at the one door every ticket write passes, not only at cast); Law 5 (trail written as an ad-hoc top-level key is the drift that grew 166 unread fields).
how: cairn/tools/artifact only. (1) jurisdiction.json: the tickets '*.json' entry gains 'keys_from': 'tickets/_charter+why.json#plan_fields'. (2) artifact.py: after the canonical check for '.json', when the matched record entry has keys_from, load that charter (resolved under the same root) and read the named list; extras = sorted(set(doc) - set(list)); refuse with Refused naming them. Records whose name starts '_' (the charter itself) are exempt by the existing name match only if the pattern excludes them; measure and, if '*.json' matches '_charter+why.json', exempt names starting '_' explicitly for keys_from. (3) A charter or field that cannot be read is a refusal too (gates are hard). Depends on 29569fca68a3 having run: before it, every v1 ticket write would be refused.
falsifier: cairn/tools/artifact/proofs/test_a_record_set_declares_its_keys.py under PROVES {'1fc53d5d96cc': {'1','2','3'}}, on a tmp root with a tmp charter: (1) a ticket body with only declared keys lands; (2) a body with one extra key is refused naming it, file and journal unchanged; (3) a missing charter or missing field refuses every write to the set; the charter file itself writes freely. Hollow: dropping the keys_from read reds 2.
watchme: none, because every ticket write after the migration 29569fca68a3 passes this door, and a refusal is loud at the writer; there is nothing slower to watch; the intention it serves is /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-a-ticket-is-a-plan-and-a-log.md

decisions.text: Keys are declared in the store's own charter and the jurisdiction only points at them, so plan_fields has one spelling (Law 1). CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09
